title: Adaptive preemption allocator for continuous batcher with KV-aware memory accounting
creator: Riley Chen
description:
Problem: The continuous batcher currently preempts inflight requests by simple LIFO or age-based heuristics. When KV cache entries and variable KV sizes are present, naive preemption can evict hot KV state or cause OOMs on GPUs because memory accounting doesn't include pinned KV residency and spilled buffers. This leads to unfairness (long requests repeatedly preempted) and tail latency regressions for customers with long contexts.

Goal: Implement an adaptive preemption allocator that: (1) maintains precise GPU memory accounting that includes KV cache residency and transient spill buffers; (2) uses a fairness-aware scoring function to pick candidate requests for preemption; (3) allows resumable/preemptible request execution (checkpoint/resume of KV indices where feasible); and (4) exposes tuning knobs and telemetry for SLO-driven rollout.

Design summary:
- Memory accounting: extend the runtime allocator to report per-request live set estimates: model weights (shared), KV-resident size (tracked per-session), current output buffer, and predicted peak for remaining tokens (based on request token budget and model profile). Use conservative upper-bounds for safety.
- Scoring function: compute preemption_cost = alpha*remaining_work + beta*kv_residency + gamma*latency_penalty + delta*customer_priority. Lower score => better candidate for preemption. Alpha/Beta/Gamma/Delta are runtime-configurable; defaults tuned to favor evicting short remaining work with low KV residency.
- Fairness: maintain per-key fairness windows so a long-running request gains protection score over repeated preemptions. Add backoff multiplier on preemption_cost after each preemption to avoid thrashing.
- Resumable preemption: where model runtime supports KV-range checkpointing, capture minimal KV index snapshot and allow preempted requests to re-enter batch queue with restored state; otherwise fall back to safe restart and increment telemetry to track restart cost.
- Spilling policy: integrate with on-device spill manager to move cold KV pages to host RAM or NVMe before preempting memory-critical requests. Prefer spilling cold sessions where eviction cost is lowest.
- Admission control: when predicted peak (including anticipated batches) exceeds a safety threshold, trigger short-term admission backpressure rather than indiscriminate preemption. This reduces tail thrash for high-priority customers.

Trade-offs considered:
- Complexity vs safety: Per-request accounting adds overhead; we will sample and extrapolate for low-cost estimates and only enable full accounting for nodes running in dedicated pools.
- Resume complexity: Checkpoint/resume reduces user-visible latency but increases runtime state management complexity and failure surfaces. We'll gate resume support behind a per-customer opt-in flag initially.

Metrics to track: p50/p95/p99 generation latency, preemption count and repeat preemptions per request, preemption-induced restarts, KV spill frequency, GPU OOMs, throughput (tokens/s) and cost per token. SLO targets: p99 gen latency regression < 10% vs baseline under 95th percentile load; preemption rate < 0.5% for tier-1 seats.

Rollout plan:
1) Simulated tester in staging: validate scoring and memory accounting under synthetic mixes (short chat, long context, embeddings).
2) Canary in dedicated pool with conservative alpha/beta defaults and resume disabled. Monitor metrics for 72h.
3) Enable KV-aware spilling and resume for a small set of customers with opt-in.
4) Gradually widen and expose tuning controls in Console (backpressure threshold, fairness window, weight params).

Deliverables: design doc (Confluence link), runtime patch (C++), controller config updates, unit/integration tests, benchmark harness, Console knobs and dashboards, rollout runbook.

Links: Confluence design: https://redwood.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/INFR/pages/Adaptive+Preemptor; PR (WIP): https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/1542; benchmark dashboard: https://grafana.redwood.ai/d/evm/kv-preemption-tests
acceptance_criteria: Per-request GPU memory accounting added and exposed to the batcher scheduler
Preemption scorer implemented and unit-tested with configurable weights
Fairness window/backoff prevents repeated preemptions of the same request in >95% synthetic runs
Spilling integration reduces OOM incidence under synthetic memory pressure scenarios
Canary rollout shows p99 latency regression < 10% and preemption rate < 0.5% for tier-1 workloads
Runbook and Console knobs published, with dashboards for preemption metrics
